catalog_quote: I.1.1. TONEMES. Le Mpumpuŋ est une langue à tons.¹⁵ Défini comme "... la hauteur relative de la voix pendant l'exécution d'un son" Wiesemann & al (1988:84), le ton y assume une fonction distinctive. Il ressort de nos investigations, les quatre tonèmes suivants: [p. 16] ... II.1 SYNTAGMATIQUE DES TONS. Le système tonal du mpumpuŋ est fait de quatre tonèmes: haut, bas, montant, descendant. Nous nous arrêtons un instant sur la situation des tons dans les monosyllabes pour ensuite appréhender les différents schémas tonématiques. [p. 50] ... En Mpumpuŋ, l'unique voie de définition de la syllabe, c'est la présence d'un tonème dont le support est une voyelle. [p. 56]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: Mpumpuŋ is a tone language. Defined as '... the relative pitch of the voice during the production of a sound' (Wiesemann et al. 1988:84), tone there has a distinctive function. Our investigations yield the following four tonemes: [p. 16] ... The tonal system of Mpumpuŋ consists of four tonemes: high, low, rising, falling. [p. 50] ... In Mpumpuŋ, the only way to define the syllable is the presence of a toneme whose bearer is a vowel. [p. 56]

new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is described as a tone language with four contrastive tonemes (H, L, LH, HL); the syllable and the phonological word are defined through tone and segments only. The description contains no statement about word stress, accent or prominence at all — neither a rule nor a denial.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described at the level of the lexeme/monosyllable and in tone sequences within di- and trisyllabic words (pp. 50-54); dialect of Yokadouma (parler de Yokadouma).
new_statements.identity_note: Djiafeua 1989 describes the 'parler de Yokadouma' (Yokadouma dialect) of Mpumpuŋ; the MPG record tags it ISO 639-3 mgg (= Glottolog mpon1254 Mpongmpong). The Wikipedia/Ethnologue 'Mpumpong' entry lists nine varieties (Mezime, Mpobyáng, Mpopó, Bagéto, Kunabeeb, Mpyámó, Mpomam, Esel, Bijugi); Ngangoum 2002 and Lebika 2003 do not name a dialect. Mpiemo (mpie1238, ISO mcx) is treated as a separate language by Glottolog and is not what these theses describe.

new_statements.quote: Djiafeua (1989) has written a dissertation on "Esquisse phonologique du Mpumpuŋ". He came out with the following conclusions. Mpumpuŋ has 7 vowels, 30 consonants and 4 main tones. The alphabet has 37 letters. [...] The syllable in Mpumpuŋ is defined as the presence of a tone on a vowel. [...] Concerning tones, it is very common to come across many simple tones in a word than to come across many modulated ones. In Mpumpuŋ, low tone is recurrent as shown in example (1).

new_statements.relation_note: Secondhand: the phonology section only restates Djiafeua 1989's conclusions (tones, vowels, consonants, syllable). It repeats the tone-language finding already in the catalog's existing statement and adds nothing on stress; the rest of the thesis is verb morphology and IP structure with tone marked on morphemes (floating H/L tones as grammatical markers).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tone language with four tones (high, low, rising, falling; Table 1 p. 7); every syllable is defined by a tone on its vowel. Nothing is said about word stress or accent anywhere in the thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent the full text, plain and scanned-space-tolerant, for stress/accent/prominence: zero hits; the phonology section pp. 7-8 read by eye).
new_statements.identity_note: Djiafeua 1989 is titled 'parler de Yokadouma' and describes the Mpumpuŋ of the Yokadouma area (Boumba-Ngoko, East Cameroon) = Glottolog mpon1254 / ISO mgg. Lebika 2003 (Yaoundé I) works on the same language and takes its phonology wholesale from Djiafeua. Cheucle 2014, per the prior theses.fr-based note (unverified here), treats eight other A80 languages and not Mpongmpong.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Full structuralist phonology of the Yokadouma variety: tone is the distinctive suprasegmental, with four tonemes (H, L, LH, HL) and tone sequences over mono- and disyllables (§II.1); the syllable is defined by a toneme on a vowel; the 'mot phonologique' (§II.2.3, p. 57) is defined only in terms of phonemes and syllables. There is no section, heading or sentence on accent, stress or intensity anywhere (TOC pp. 124-128 read by eye; a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned layer, plain and space-tolerant, for accent/intensité/proéminence/prosod/stress: zero hits; conclusion p. 118 and notes p. 120 read by eye).

sources.note: The PHOIBLE inventory PH 945 for Mpumpun, coded from Djiafeua 1989, lists 38 segments: 29 consonants, 7 vowels (a e ɛ i o ɔ u) and 2 tones, high ˦ and low ˨; Djiafeua's rising and falling tonemes are not entered as separate units, so the database registers a two-level tone system.
